new_bugs.title: A legitimate first payment is refunded as 'already cancelled' when the checkout message and the paid-invoice message overlap
new_bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts settleInvoice() lines 746 to 751 and adopt() lines 414 to 442
new_bugs.detail: Steps (tests/out/verify-billing-terms/p1-activation.ts, 'RACE checkout-first' and 'B6 race'): new account; stripe.delayMs = 20; start applyStripeEvent(checkout.session.completed) and 5 ms later applyStripeEvent(invoice.paid) for the same subscription. Result: plan grove, balance 3 (no signatures added), payment row credits 0 / refunded_cents 900, $9.00 refunded at the provider, emails 'Welcome to Grove' then 'Refund sent: $9.00', plan history 'Refund sent: $9.00: this plan was already cancelled', subscription left active. Same for a returning subscriber. In the opposite order, and with the browser's /billing/sync in the mix, nothing is refunded but 'Welcome to Grove' is sent twice and 'Monthly plan started' is logged twice. Why: both paths read the account before waiting for the provider; whichever resumes second sees the subscription already adopted, adopt() returns false, and settleInvoice() treats false as 'should never have been charged'. The real provider sends both messages within the same second, and each handler waits for a provider call, so this will hit a large share of new subscribers. Fix: in settleInvoice(), after adopt(), re-read the account and refund only if it is still not on subscription S (or S is not alive); make adopt() re-read the account after its provider call, change the row with one conditional UPDATE, and send the welcome only when that UPDATE changed a row. Add a test with stripe.delayMs and Promise.all in both orders.

new_bugs.title: A card dispute returns the money and leaves every signature in place (up to 500 per top-up), automatically
new_bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts handleEvent(), charge.dispute.created, lines 967 to 985
new_bugs.detail: Steps (p3-refunds.ts 'DISPUTE'): subscribe, top up 500 signatures for $500.00 (balance 512), deliver charge.dispute.created for the top-up's charge. Result: the dispute is closed in the customer's favour by the software (disputes/dp_big/close), payment marked $500.00 refunded, balance still 512 available, a new envelope still sends (200), email says 'the signatures you have stay yours' and 'you can start the plan again from the Plan page at any time'. Anyone can repeat this: pay, dispute, keep the signatures, start again; the business also pays the bank's dispute fee each time. Fix: when a dispute is accepted, take back the unused signatures of that payment (the same sum a refund would take), pause sending for a person to review when used signatures exceed what was paid for, and do not offer to start again without review. Consider not auto-accepting disputes on top-ups.

stripe_doubts.what: A top-up created with invoice_creation[enabled]=true makes Stripe create and pay an Invoice, and send invoice.paid for it (billing_reason 'manual'). The code treats that as a second payment.
stripe_doubts.why: Post-payment invoices from Checkout are ordinary Invoice objects and go through the normal invoice events; the README tells the operator to subscribe to invoice.paid. The stand-in never emits events on its own, so no test sees it. Simulated in p4-code-tools.ts 'TOPINV': double row, mangroves 290 instead of 190, false operator alert.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Mark the invoice at checkout with invoice_creation[invoice_data][metadata][kind]=topup and return early from settleInvoice() for it (store only its link on the top-up row), or match on the charge/payment already recorded.

stripe_doubts.what: Newer API versions (2025-03-31 'basil' and later, the default for a new Stripe account) no longer put charge or payment_intent on the Invoice, nor invoice on the Charge. chargeOf() then finds nothing and chargeTarget() refunds 'the newest unrefunded charge of the same amount'.
stripe_doubts.why: The code reads invoice.payments only if it is expanded, and webhook payloads are not expanded. Simulated in p5-more.ts 'SAME AMOUNT': monthly payment in the new shape (understood: plan on, 12 signatures) plus a $9 top-up; refunding the monthly payment sent the refund to the top-up's charge (ch_cs_same_top), and the monthly charge was never refunded. The stand-in then allowed a second refund on the same charge because it tracks charge and payment_intent separately; the real API refuses it ('already refunded'), so the second refund would fail for the customer.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: When a payment has no charge on record, fetch it: GET /v1/invoice_payments?invoice=in_... (or GET the invoice with expand[]=payments) and store the payment_intent. Never match by amount when more than one candidate exists. Send a Stripe-Version header so the shape is known.

stripe_doubts.what: The idempotency key on refunds makes the timer's retries return the first failure again for 24 hours.
stripe_doubts.why: Stripe stores the first result for a key, including 5xx and most 4xx answers produced after the request started executing, and replays it for 24 hours. The retry in billingRetries() uses the same key (sg-refund-<payment>-<refunded>-<cents>). With the 40-try limit and a timer that runs hourly or more often, a refund that failed once at Stripe gets one or two real attempts in total, then is dropped.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Before retrying, list refunds for the charge (GET /v1/refunds?charge=...) to see whether it already exists; if not, retry with a key that includes the attempt day. Remove the 40-try limit or alert again when it is reached.

stripe_doubts.what: Checkout may charge a top-up in the customer's own currency (Adaptive Pricing); session.amount_total and session.currency are then in that currency.
stripe_doubts.why: applyTopUp() caps the signatures at floor(amount_total / 100), assuming US cents. Simulated in p1-activation.ts: 10 signatures paid as GBP 7.90 are credited as 7 ('Receipt: £7.90 for 7 signatures'). Whether this happens depends on the account's Adaptive Pricing setting, which is on by default for many accounts.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Send adaptive_pricing[enabled]=false on both checkouts, or read the merchant-currency amount from session.currency_conversion and refuse a top-up whose currency is not usd.

stripe_doubts.what: DELETE /v1/subscriptions/{id} on a subscription that is already cancelled returns an error, not the subscription.
stripe_doubts.why: routes-billing.ts handles this ('No such subscription' counts as gone, else it re-reads the status). routes-trust.ts POST /me/delete does not: any non-2xx answer blocks closing. I believe Stripe answers 404 resource_missing here; the stand-in does the same. If Stripe instead answers 400 with another message, endSubscription() still copes through its GET, but closing an account stays blocked.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Use stopBillingFor() in POST /me/delete.

stripe_doubts.what: 'Remove card' and stop-by-card with an email only look at payment methods of type card.
stripe_doubts.why: Checkout offers Link, wallets and bank debits depending on dashboard settings. Those are not listed by GET /v1/payment_methods?type=card. POST /billing/remove-card then answers {removed: 0} (p3-refunds.ts 'CARD') and the page still prints 'Card removed. Nothing can be charged to it.'; stop-by-card with an email cannot match such a payer at all.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: List without the type filter and detach everything; say so on the page when nothing was removed; set payment_method_types=['card'] on the checkouts if only cards are wanted.

stripe_doubts.what: The charge search used by stop-by-card and the operator lookup.
stripe_doubts.why: Query sent: payment_method_details.card.last4:9911 AND status:'succeeded' AND created>... AND created<... AND amount:900. The fields exist in Stripe's search language as far as I know, but: digits are sent unquoted, so last four digits starting with 0 may be read as a number; search is not available in every region and lags behind real time by up to a minute or more; only the first 50 results are read (has_more is ignored); errors are swallowed and reported as 'details do not match'. The stand-in ignores the date entirely (a charge date of 2019-01-01 stopped a plan in p4-code-tools.ts), so the date window has never been exercised.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Quote the value (last4:"0042"), page through results, return 502 on failure, and try it in test mode before launch.

stripe_doubts.what: Webhook signature check during a secret roll.
stripe_doubts.why: While a rolled secret is kept alive Stripe sends one v1 signature per secret in the same header. verifyStripeSignature() keeps only the last v1 (Object.fromEntries). p5-more.ts 'WEBHOOK': good signature first and another after it: 400; good one last: 200. Every delivery could be refused for up to 24 hours after rolling the secret.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Collect all v1 values and accept if any matches.

stripe_doubts.what: The top-up's invoice link.
stripe_doubts.why: applyTopUp() reads s.invoice from checkout.session.completed. With invoice_creation the invoice is made after the payment, and I am not sure the id is already in that message. If it is not, the receipt has no invoice link, and a later /billing/sync cannot add it because the function returns as soon as the row exists (p4-code-tools.ts 'TOPLINK': receipt_url stays null).
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Store the link when the invoice's own message arrives, or when sync sees an invoice on a row that has none.

stripe_doubts.what: A cancellation expressed as cancel_at (a date) instead of cancel_at_period_end.
stripe_doubts.why: The dashboard's 'cancel on a date' and possibly newer portal versions set cancel_at. The handler only reads cancel_at_period_end, so the Plan page shows the plan as renewing and the timer sends 'Heads up: your plan renews on ... for $9.00' for a plan that will end (p5-more.ts 'PORTAL cancel_at').
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Treat a cancel_at in the future as a planned end too.

stripe_doubts.what: No timeout and no pinned API version on calls to Stripe; network failures surface as a generic error.
stripe_doubts.why: stripe() uses fetch with no AbortSignal and no Stripe-Version header. When the host cannot be reached fetch throws, which is not an HttpError, so the customer sees 'Something went wrong on our side ...' instead of the careful 'the payment provider did not confirm' texts (seen in the browser run: Cancel plan and the stop page, with no provider reachable). A hanging connection holds the request and the webhook open.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Add AbortSignal.timeout(15000), catch network errors in stripe() and throw bad(..., 502), and send a fixed Stripe-Version.

new_bugs.title: First payment is refunded as 'this plan was already cancelled' when two provider messages are handled at the same moment
new_bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts, settleInvoice() lines 746 to 752 ('if (!(await adopt(...))) why = ...') and adopt() line 418
new_bugs.detail: Steps: new account, paid checkout. Deliver invoice.paid and customer.subscription.updated (status active) for the new subscription so that they overlap (probe: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/tests/out/verify-billing-core/p7-more.ts, provider answering in 5 ms, Promise.all of the two messages). The invoice handler reads the account (no subscription yet) and waits for GET subscriptions/S. Meanwhile the other message adopts the subscription. When the invoice handler continues, adopt() returns false because the account is already on S, and the code reads 'false' as 'this subscription should not exist'. Result, 10 runs out of 10: payments.refunded_cents=900, credits=0, balance 3 instead of 12, $9.00 sent back at the provider, mails 'Welcome to Grove' then 'Refund sent: $9.00 ... (this plan was already cancelled)', plan shown Active with a next charge. Same with checkout message + browser sync + invoice together (p1-order.ts race C, where sync even answers applied:'plan'), and for a returning customer (p8-last.ts). One after the other, in either order: no refund. After a real checkout the provider sends these messages within the same second, so this is the common case, not a corner. Fix: make adopt() return three answers (adopted now, already on it, refused) or, after a false, re-read the account and treat stripe_subscription_id === S with a live status as fine. Better still, take a per-account lock (or run the whole decision in one transaction after all provider reads) so two messages for one account never interleave. Add a test with stripe.delayMs and Promise.all.

stripe_doubts.what: Monthly payments will have no charge id on current API versions, and the fallback picks a charge by amount
stripe_doubts.why: From API version 2025-03-31 (basil) the Invoice object has no 'charge' and no 'payment_intent'; they moved to invoice payments, and 'payments' is only present when expanded, which webhook payloads are not. chargeOf() (routes-billing.ts line 64) reads o.charge, o.payment_intent and o.payments.data[0], so it returns null and every plan payment is stored with charge_id NULL. chargeTarget() then lists the customer's last 20 charges and takes the first paid, not fully refunded one with the same amount, guarded by '!c.invoice || c.invoice === p.id'; the same version removed 'invoice' from Charge, so the guard passes for every charge. Probe p4-refunds.ts 'B8 angle': plan $9 then a 9-signature top-up ($9): refunding the plan payment refunded the top-up's charge. The stand-in then also allowed the top-up refund (it counts refunds by charge and by payment intent separately); the real API would refuse it as already refunded, so the customer is $9 short and the plan charge is never refunded. The author already handles the other basil moves (period end on items, parent.subscription_details), so this version is the target.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: When the invoice arrives, call GET /v1/invoice_payments?invoice=<id> (or GET /v1/invoices/<id>?expand[]=payments) and store the payment intent in payments.charge_id. Keep the amount match only as a last resort and restrict it to charges whose payment intent is not already tied to another payments row. Make the stand-in share one refunded total per charge.

stripe_doubts.what: Every top-up also produces an invoice.paid message, which is recorded as a second payment
stripe_doubts.why: The top-up checkout sets invoice_creation[enabled]=true. Stripe then creates and pays an invoice for the one-off payment and sends invoice.paid for it with billing_reason 'manual'. settleInvoice() matches it by customer, stores it as kind 'other' with 0 signatures and alerts operators. Probe p4-refunds.ts 'NEW (provider behaviour)': after a $9 plan payment and a $5 top-up the payments list has three rows (the extra one shows as 'Monthly plan, 0 signatures, $5.00'), the Plan page says 190 mangroves instead of 140, the public total is inflated, the alert 'An invoice that is not the monthly plan was paid' fires for each top-up, and after refunding the top-up the page still counts the phantom $5. The extra row is also the latest payment, so the 'Want your money back?' card disappears after any top-up. The stand-in never sends this message.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: In settleInvoice(), before inserting, look for a top-up row with the same payment intent or with the session whose 'invoice' is this id and attach the receipt link to it instead of creating a row. Or drop invoice_creation and link the charge's receipt_url.

stripe_doubts.what: At a renewal the provider reports the new period first and takes the money about an hour later
stripe_doubts.why: Stripe creates the renewal invoice as a draft at the period boundary, sends customer.subscription.updated with the new period end, and finalises and charges the invoice roughly an hour later. Three effects, each shown by a probe that plays the messages in that order: (a) settleInvoice() compares renewal_reminded with renews_at after renews_at has already moved a month on, so 'renewed without a reminder going out first' is raised for a renewal that was reminded twice (p3-timers.ts 'Reminder angle 1'); (b) a customer who cancels in that hour is told 'the plan runs until <next month>, because that month is already paid for', then charged, and the charge is kept (p2-cancel.ts 'B4 angle 3'); (c) the Plan page line 'Next charge: $9.00 on December 2, 2026 at 10:35 AM ... cancel right up to the charge' names the period end, not the charge.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Do the reminder check against the invoice's own period start (lines.data[0].period.start), not accounts.renews_at. In cancelPlan(), when the latest invoice of the subscription is draft or open, end the subscription now and void that invoice, or say plainly that one more payment is in progress. Show the charge time as 'about an hour after'.

stripe_doubts.what: The upcoming-invoice message quotes the attempt time, about an hour after the period end, and the reminder marker is keyed on that
stripe_doubts.why: handleEvent uses o.next_payment_attempt || o.period_end. On upcoming invoices next_payment_attempt is the period end plus about an hour. The marker 'YYYY-MM-DD|stages' is the UTC date of whichever time was passed in, while the timer uses renews_at (the period end). For a period that ends between 23:00 and 24:00 UTC the two dates differ. Probe p3-timers.ts 'Reminder angle 3': three 'Heads up' mails for one renewal, dated Nov 25, Nov 26, Nov 25.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Use o.period_end for the reminder key and for the date in the mail, and key the marker on the subscription period end stored on the account.

stripe_doubts.what: Refund retries reuse one idempotency key, and the provider replays the first answer for that key, errors included
stripe_doubts.why: refundPayment() sends 'sg-refund-<payment>-<refunded so far>-<cents>'. Stripe documents that it saves the status and body of the first request for a key once the endpoint started executing, and returns the same result for 24 hours, including 500s. A first attempt that fails for a passing reason (not enough balance at the provider, an internal error) is therefore replayed on every retry. Probe p7-more.ts with a wrapper that behaves that way: 41 tries, one key, tries=40, refunded 0. The stand-in remembers keys only for successes. Second half: keys are forgotten after 24 hours, so a retry later than that after a lost answer would pay a partial refund twice.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Keep the same key only for retries after a network error or timeout. After a definite error answer use a new key (for example add the try number) and first check GET /v1/refunds?charge=... for an existing refund of that amount. Remove the 40-try cap or alert again when it is reached.

stripe_doubts.what: Deleting or updating a subscription that is already cancelled is an error at the provider
stripe_doubts.why: endSubscription() copes with it ('No such subscription' or a GET that says canceled). Two places do not. POST /me/delete in routes-trust.ts treats any non-200 as 'could not stop your subscription', so a former payer on the free code can never close (probe, with the stand-in, which also answers 404). POST /billing/resume updates cancel_at_period_end=false on a subscription that may already be gone; the stand-in accepts that and the page turns Active (p3-timers.ts 'Stuck'), while Stripe answers 400 that a canceled subscription can only update its cancellation details and metadata, which would reach the customer as a raw 502 message.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Use endOrQueue() in /me/delete. In resume, on an error re-read the subscription and, if it is cancelled, mark the account ended and tell the customer to start the plan again.

stripe_doubts.what: Webhook signature check fails while the signing secret is being rolled
stripe_doubts.why: verifyStripeSignature() builds an object from the header parts, so with two v1 values only the last survives. Stripe sends one v1 per active secret during a roll. Probe p6-misc.ts: header 'v1=<new>,v1=<old>' with the new secret: false; the other order: true. While it fails every message gets 400 and is retried.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Collect all v1 values and accept if any matches.

stripe_doubts.what: A cancellation made in the provider portal may arrive as 'cancel_at' and not as 'cancel_at_period_end'
stripe_doubts.why: The code reads only cancel_at_period_end (lines 430 and 943). Newer billing modes and the portal can express 'ends at the end of the period' as a cancel_at timestamp. If so, the Plan page keeps saying Active, reminders say 'we will charge $9.00', and the plan then simply ends. I could not confirm which field the portal sets on the account's API version.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Treat a non-null o.cancel_at as set to end at that time, in adopt() and in the subscription branch.

stripe_doubts.what: 'Remove card' only removes cards
stripe_doubts.why: GET /v1/payment_methods is called with type=card. Checkout in subscription mode can save other methods (Link, bank debits) depending on dashboard settings. Probe p6-misc.ts: with no card on file the answer is removed:0 and the page still shows 'Card removed. Nothing can be charged to it.'
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: List without a type filter (or per enabled type), detach all, and word the result from the count.

stripe_doubts.what: Charge search for 'stop by card' and the operator lookup
stripe_doubts.why: The query syntax (payment_method_details.card.last4:4242 AND status:'succeeded' AND created>.. AND amount:900) matches the documented search fields and uses only AND. Search data is eventually consistent (a charge from the last minute can be missing) and the Search API is not offered in every region. The stand-in ignores the date clauses, so the window of minus 2 to plus 3 days is untested. README already calls this the least certain part.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Test once in Stripe test mode; on an empty result within a few minutes of a charge, say 'try again in a few minutes'.

stripe_doubts.what: Zero-amount and tiny invoices
stripe_doubts.why: applyInvoice() ignores an invoice with amount_paid 0 (a coupon or customer credit at the provider): the plan turns on, 'Welcome to Grove' says '$9.00 a month adds 9 signatures ... with every payment', and no signatures arrive that month (p6-misc.ts). An invoice under $1 sends 'Receipt: $0.99 for 0 signatures' and cannot be refunded in the app. Both need a coupon, credit or proration at the provider, which the app never creates itself.
stripe_doubts.suggested_fix: Decide the rule: either grant the month's signatures for a paid-in-full $0 invoice of the plan price, or alert operators; refund sub-dollar invoices automatically.
